The Turkish Football Federation’s disciplinary committee has banned 147 current and former club officials for 45 days for violating betting rules, following an investigation into gambling in Turkish football. The Professional Football Disciplinary Board imposed the penalties on Tuesday after reviewing the cases of 448 officials referred by the federation over allegations they had placed bets while serving at clubs, Reuters reported. “The committee found that 147 out of 448 individuals had violated betting rules and imposed 45-day penalties, which bar football officials from carrying out duties within the sport during the suspension period,” Reuters reported. Those sanctioned included Ertugrul Dogan, president of Turkish Super Lig club Trabzonspor, according to the committee’s ruling. However, the board cleared the remaining officials, with Reuters reporting that “the board imposed no penalties in the other 301 cases after finding insufficient grounds for disciplinary action.” So This Happened (EP 436): MC Alger fans allegedly damage stadium after defeat to Enugu Rangers 12 migrants die in Aegean Sea crossings – Greek coast guard EPL: I”ll be back in few weeks, says Chelsea goal keeper Martinez The Turkish Football Federation (TFF) had announced in September that it had provisionally suspended 448 current and former club officials who had served at clubs competing in the country’s top two divisions over the previous five years. “The federation said at the time that those referred had been found to have placed bets while holding club positions,” the outlet reported. The latest sanctions form part of the federation’s efforts to strengthen oversight of betting in Turkish football. “The TFF has tightened its oversight of betting since a scandal rocked Turkish soccer,” the agency reported.
